questions.stem: A strawberry plant sends out runners that grow into new plants. A gardener notices that all the new plants are identical to the parent. Which best explains why this is an advantage in a stable environment?

options.text: The offspring have greater genetic variation to cope with disease
The offspring are all well-suited to the current conditions since they share the parent's successful genotype
The offspring will grow faster because they are produced by meiosis
The offspring can resist any new predators that enter the habitat

questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction produces genetically identical offspring (clones). In a stable environment, this is advantageous because the parent's genotype is already well-adapted to those conditions, so all offspring will be too. However, this lack of variation becomes a disadvantage if the environment changes.

questions.stem: A population of organisms that only reproduces asexually is exposed to a new fungal disease. What is the most likely outcome for this population?

options.text: Only a few individuals will be affected because they vary genetically
The population will quickly evolve resistance through natural selection
Most or all individuals could be affected because they are genetically identical
The population will switch to sexual reproduction to produce resistant offspring

questions.explanation: Since asexual reproduction produces clones with no genetic variation, if one individual is susceptible to the disease, all are likely susceptible. This is a major disadvantage of asexual reproduction. Sexual reproduction would give variation, meaning some individuals might be naturally resistant.

questions.stem: Aphids reproduce asexually during summer but switch to sexual reproduction in autumn before winter. What is the most likely biological advantage of this strategy?

options.text: Sexual reproduction is faster, allowing rapid population growth before winter
Asexual reproduction in summer allows rapid population growth, while sexual reproduction in autumn produces variation to survive the changing winter conditions
Sexual reproduction requires less energy than asexual reproduction
The aphids switch to sexual reproduction because they run out of food for asexual reproduction

questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction is faster and requires only one parent, enabling rapid population growth in favourable summer conditions. Switching to sexual reproduction before the harsh, unpredictable winter generates genetic variation, increasing the chance that some offspring will survive the changed conditions.

questions.stem: A farmer wants to produce a large number of identical crop plants as quickly as possible. Which method of reproduction should they use?

options.text: Cross-pollination between two different varieties
Collecting and planting seeds from the best plants
Taking cuttings and growing them into new plants
Allowing self-pollination to occur naturally

questions.explanation: Taking cuttings is a form of asexual reproduction that produces genetically identical plants (clones) quickly. Cross-pollination and seed production involve sexual reproduction, which introduces genetic variation and takes longer. The farmer needs identical plants fast, so asexual reproduction via cuttings is ideal.

questions.stem: Daffodils can reproduce both by producing seeds and by growing new bulbs from the parent bulb. Which statement correctly compares these two methods?

options.text: Both methods involve meiosis and produce genetically varied offspring
Seed production involves mitosis only, while bulb division involves meiosis
Seed production involves meiosis and fusion of gametes, producing variation; bulb division involves mitosis, producing clones
Bulb division produces more genetic variation than seed production

questions.explanation: Seed production is sexual reproduction: it involves meiosis to form gametes (pollen and egg cells), which fuse at fertilisation, producing genetically varied offspring. Bulb division is asexual reproduction: it involves mitosis only, producing genetically identical offspring (clones) of the parent plant.
